Alyssa / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment on pilot goals. Per our conversation, summarized below are the suggested capacity allocation and pricing targets we think will let Greenline prove value while keeping the pilot affordable. Please review and confirm which items you want included in the SOW. I attached a brief pilot_scope.xlsx with the per-route volume assumptions.

Quick recap (from call):
- Pilot duration: 6 weeks active / 2 weeks ramp-down
- Expected average daily requests: ~45k requests/day (spiky)
- Typical payload: chat prompts ~400 tokens in / 300 tokens out; embeddings 1k tokens per request (batching assumed); rerank payloads small (~50 tokens per item)
- Success metrics: 80% reduction in time-to-insight, initial latency SLOs under 400ms p50 for chat test-case, embeddings throughput target 500 qps during batch windows

Recommended pilot composition (Redwood suggested):
- Chat (conversational + system prompts): 55% of total tokens
- Embeddings (vector storage + search): 30% of total tokens
- Rerank / lightweight NLP: 15% of total tokens

Token economics & price targets (pilot level, non-production):
- Target blended bill target: $1,000 per 1M tokens (goal range: $700 — $1,300 depending on batching and cache share)
- Example per-model guidance for the pilot (illustrative):
  - Chat (gpt-like open variant): expected unit cost ~ $1,200 / 1M tokens without KV cache; with prefix caching & batching we estimate effective ~$800 / 1M tokens
  - Embeddings (dense vector generator): expected compute-heavy per-call; target ~$1,400 / 1M tokens but amortized across batched calls could fall to ~$600 / 1M tokens if batched and cached
  - Rerank (small transformer): target ~$300 / 1M tokens

Notes on lowering cost during pilot:
- Prefer caching common system prompts and reuse of KV cache for chat sessions to reduce forward pass compute
- Use mixed precision quantized variants for embedding generator to decrease GPU time; Redwood can provision quantized SKU during pilot
- Set traffic routing to prioritize cheaper model variant for non-critical flows (e.g., background analytics)

Action items / asks for Greenline:
1) Confirm ballpark monthly token budget for pilot (choose one): <$5M, $5M–$15M, >$15M
2) Share a representative sample of 1k chat requests + 1k embedding requests (anonymized) for our perf run
3) Confirm whether rerank traffic can be batched into periodic jobs or needs online low-latency behavior
4) Approve the pilot SOW outline (attached) so we can lock capacity and pricing windows

I will follow up with a short SOW and a simple interactive worksheet that maps your chosen budget band to expected throughput and model mix.

Thanks,
Irene

Alyssa — quick answers inline.

> Can you call out what the expected latency impact would be if we route 30% of chat traffic to a cheaper model variant (lower quality) as a fallback?

- In most cases, cheaper variants drop ~20–40ms p50 but can increase tail latency if under heavy KV cache miss patterns. For interactive UIs where UX is sensitive, we recommend fallback for non-critical paths (e.g., summarization, system prompts). For your 400/300 token profile, expect p95 to move +60–120ms for requests that hit the fallback and +10–20ms for ones served by the primary variant.

> single-line estimate for total pilot cost at the mid-point of our budget (~8M tokens/month) using the suggested model mix?

- Using the suggested mix (55/30/15) and pilot discounts for reserved capacity, rough blended estimate: $6,400 / month (pilot), which maps to ~ $800 / 1M tokens effective. This assumes: 20% effective saving from batching on embeddings windows and 10% saving from KV caching on chat.

I'll attach a simple worked example in the SOW spreadsheet (see the pilot_scope.xlsx Irene attached).

Karthik

Alyssa / team — adding a note from pricing side. A couple of guardrails we typically include in pilot SOWs to keep spend predictable: 

- Flat-rate weekly caps with overage alerts (we can set email + webhook hooks at 80% and 95%)
- Per-route soft limits (e.g., limit rerank to 150 qps during pilot; we can bump for brief load tests)
- Pre-agreed fallback routing rules (if p50 latency > 800ms route to fallback variant)

On the unit economics: our pilot discount structure for reserved pilot capacity is tiered; mid-point (8M tokens/mo) usually receives a 20% pilot discount off hosted list. That aligns the blended figure Karthik gave (~$800 / 1M tokens). If you want a strict target (for internal procurement), we can set an anchor at $750 / 1M tokens as a negotiation starting point and then reconcile after perf validation.

Happy to include an explicit cost table in the SOW.

—Rishi
